evidence.reason: The alleged failure needs a retained pending file whose payload changes while its id stays the same after a successful push. No intended code path produces that state: `Outbox.spool` writes each event to `pending/<id>.json` only after refusing a same-id file with different content (`if filename.exists() and loads(filename.read_bytes()) != value: raise IntegrityError("outbox replay conflict")`, lines 537-541), and `retained()` documents the pending store as content-addressed and immutable (lines 544-550). A replay is the same bytes that were already pushed, so acknowledging it by id matches the remote record. Reaching the described mismatch requires an out-of-band edit of the local pending file, i.e. local-filesystem tampering of an ostensibly immutable, content-addressed record; the current contract treats such forgeability/writability by an owner credential as a recorded limit or advisory rather than a defect (contract item 14). Adding a fetch-and-compare of every retained payload against remote history before ack would enlarge the protection scope (a new integrity gate and error surface) rather than repair an implementation error in existing intended behavior. The remote history remains correct even in the posited tamper scenario, so this is a hardening opportunity, not a current obligation.
